title: Messages that survive
summary: Remove the container and the messages are gone. Keep them in a volume so they outlive any container.

tasks.title: A volume called `messages` exists
tasks.hint: `docker volume create messages`, or let `docker run -v messages:...` make it for you.

tasks.title: `keeper` runs `msg-keeper` with `messages` mounted at `/app/data`
tasks.hint: `docker run -d --name keeper -p 8099:8080 -v messages:/app/data msg-keeper`. The left side of `-v` is the volume, the right side is the folder inside the container.

tasks.title: A message is saved in the volume
tasks.hint: Open http://localhost:8099/web, write a message and press Send. Then press Check: it remembers which container you used.

tasks.title: After removing `keeper` and starting a new one, the message is still there
tasks.hint: First pass the task above. Then `docker rm -f keeper`, run the same `docker run` again, and press Check.
